ops.entry: WHEN planning a semantics-preserving refactor DO record baseline exit, stdout and stderr receipts for its owning suites and state the contract from the move's guarantee (unchanged rules per physical file, real-tree equivalence), evidenced by a pre-signature census of per-file analysis state. Enumerated difference lists gain a member each cycle.
ops.why: A verbatim-move contract stated as an enumerated list of admitted output differences (field-keyed, then printed-locator, then first-site) missed one forced member per panel cycle through three reads and two post-signature amendments; it terminated only when re-anchored on what the move proves, with a per-file state census as evidence. The old P-14's 'permit only enumerated divergences' prescribed the failing shape.

ops.entry: WHEN a verify binds a receipt to a checkpoint commit DO require the recorded commit to resolve, be an ancestor, and carry content excluding both the base and later commits: hash prefixes bind nothing, and ancestry alone admits every earlier and later state.
ops.why: A receipt bound by HEAD/blob prefixes was ruled unbound by the panel and cost a cycle; the fix needed rev-parse plus ancestry plus a two-sided content predicate. Receipt-binding verifies recur in pm-authored plans far more often than installed-runtime provenance, the displaced entry's situation.

originals.original: WHEN planning a semantics-preserving refactor DO record baseline exit, stdout, and stderr receipts for every suite that owns the observable contract; permit only enumerated, bounded divergences, each with a red-first proof and an explicit ruling.

WHEN execution uses an installed or bundled runtime DO record invocation-time launcher path, version and executable hash separately from source-suite checkout and release-tag metadata. Source provenance cannot identify the binary that actually ran; label unmeasured identity rather than infer equivalence.

ops.entry: WHEN revising a field of an existing task or decision DO expect apply to replace it in place (REPLACED, exit 0); only a differing plain top-level key exits 7. For a signed task's intent, files or verify use amend --expect-sha256 --reason, which ledgers the change INV-40 otherwise reports.
ops.why: C7 verify-or-drop: control-plane plan_merge/union.py _carry_base_items replaces differing task/decision fields field by field (comment: 'This was exit 7 CONFLICT'); _merge_plain_key raises exit 7 only for a top-level key with two values; amend.py requires --reason on a signed task's intent/files/verify (INV-40 d). Old claim stale; absorbs P-08.
C7: its premise (apply exits 7 CONFLICT on any changed value) is false at union.py _carry_base_items; the surviving amend guidance is absorbed into P-04.

ops.entry: WHEN writing plan.yaml's panel key DO use record-panel from the validator lead's digest, never apply: panel is a plain top-level key, so apply exits 7 CONFLICT on any differing value. set-panel is the validated hand route, for a ruled repair only.
ops.why: C7 check of G-07: panel still routes through union.py _merge_plain_key (exit 7 on differing value), confirmed. Its set-panel safe_dump byte-churn clause is stale (set-panel now keeps unchanged findings' bytes per --help) and record-panel is the sanctioned writer (DEC-229).

ops.entry: WHEN proving a harness bin gate behaves the same before and after a change DO run both sides from a git archive of the base, the candidate overlaying only HEAD's bin and tests, with HARNESS_PROJECT_DIR set to each archive: identical plans and corpus leave only the code varying.
ops.why: Measured this feature: the archive is a runnable matched tree for check-plan-routes.py in all modes, and it removed the corpus difference (the feature's own plan exists only at pin) that otherwise polluted old-vs-new comparison. Equivalence proofs for gate refactors recur in this repo.

originals.original: WHEN widening an existing task's `files:` or `depends_on:` DO use `plan-merge.py amend --field <list> --yaml-value` with `--expect-sha256`. `apply` exits 7 CONFLICT on any changed value, so a new task id is not the only route.

WHEN revising an existing task or decision value DO use plan-merge amend --expect-sha256 --value-file, never apply, which exits 7 CONFLICT on any changed value. amend preserves the original scalar form, so the value file holds the raw body, not a re-quoted YAML value.

WHEN writing plan.yaml's panel key DO use set-panel --value-file: apply unions tasks and decisions only and exits 7 CONFLICT on panel, and set-panel re-emits the block through safe_dump, so wrapping moves even where values do not — diff loaded values, never bytes.
